zoe: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete decision on the selector for 'query aggregation' (what we've been calling grouped vs multi-query) kernels. RFC left some levers open, and ops saw a regression in p95 for short-chat workloads.

matt: I saw the regression. Short summary: multi-query gives better single-request latency on bursts but grouped-query is more cost-efficient at scale for medium-length sessions. We need deterministic tie-breakers and a fallback that doesn't thundering-herd GPU memory.

raj: +1 on deterministic ties. Also: current selector uses a simple heuristic based on avg_seq_len and q_count. That misses cases where prefix KV cache hits change the economics.

zoe: Right — cache hits matter a lot. If a request has high prefix reuse we should bias to grouped-query because KV reuse amortizes attention compute. If no reuse, multi-query often wins.

elena: Can we get an inexpensive estimator for prefix reuse? We tried sampling headers but measuring at request time adds latency.

kai: Idea: maintain a per-session rolling hit-rate metric in the router for the last N calls (N=5). Router already keeps small metadata; use that to prefer grouped-query when hit_rate > 0.6.

matt: That seems reasonable. Two follow-ups: 1) how do we ensure the runtime-side kernel can accept both inputs without recompiling? 2) what's the fallback if the kernel OOMs mid-request?

raj: For 1) the kernels share a common attention ABI in the runtime RFC. We need a tiny adapter that pads/reorders tensors. Cost of padding is small for short batches. We should document adapter microbenchmarks.

zoe: For 2) fallback flow: if grouped-query OOMs, we should transparently re-route the in-flight request to multi-query variant with conservative batching (and log a structured event). No user-visible error unless both fail.

elena: Agree. Need to avoid double-execution side-effects. For streaming responses we must resume from the last emitted token. That implies the runtime needs token-atomic checkpointing before kernel handoff.

kai: infra-bot: deploy queued: runtime/selector-v2 -> canary in us-west-2 at 15:00 UTC

matt: @kai thanks. One more tradeoff: affinity. If we sticky-route a session to a kernel variant based on history, we get better cache locality but risk load imbalance. Suggest making affinity soft: prefer but allow preemption if latency SLOs degrade.

raj: Soft affinity + preemption is good. Preemption policy: if a node's 95th latency > target and queueing > X ms, allow up to M sessions to be reassigned per minute.

zoe: I'll draft the precise preemption thresholds. Also we should add a feature flag to enable prefix-hit bias per customer (enterprise customers might want predictable deduction to multi-query to match SLAs).

elena: Tests we need: microbench for adapter padding, end-to-end canary with short-chat and long-batch corpora, and a regression test that injects synthetic prefix reuse to validate bias decisions.

matt: Ops telemetry: add a tag in traces: selector.choice={grouped|multi|fallback}, selector.reason={seqlen,qcount,prefix_hit,affinity,oom}. That will make analysis easy.

kai: infra-bot: canary scheduled: runtime/selector-v2 -> us-west-2 at 15:00 UTC (confirmed)

zoe: I'll put a short RFC follow-up doc in the repo: decision, flags, telemetry, tests. Action items:
- zoe: write RFC follow-up + test plan (due EOD tomorrow)
- matt: adapter microbench and ABI checklist (due +3d)
- raj: implement prefix hit estimator in router (PR +2d)
- elena: streaming checkpoint design + tests (due +4d)
- kai: monitor & canary rollout (in flight)

matt: Thanks. One last nit: add a numbered runbook for manual rollback if fallback cascade happens. Keep it >2 people to approve.

zoe: noted. tagging @matt @raj @elena for visibility. I'll push the draft in #eng-runtime when done. :party-parrot:

elena: +1. Thanks everyone.
